author: IGN
description:
Fields of Mistria 1.0 reviewed by Jess Reyes, played on PC.

"Fields of Mistria is the most fun I’ve had playing a farming sim since Rune Factory 4, which was the last time I remember villagers having as detailed personal lives as they do in Mistria. The level of care that NPC Studio has put into its characters and the moments that make Mistria feel like a lived-in town is vast, and I was consistently surprised throughout my 80-plus hours with how they made everyday life and its interactions undeniably charming. Minor shortcomings like interactions in the relationship process not being as fleshed out don't overshadow what it does so well. It also gives you the reins to min-max your farm, decorate, and collect to your heart’s content with few restrictions, and makes sure you don't have that nagging feeling like you're falling behind if you decide to focus on one thing at a time. I can only look forward to NPC Studio’s future additions, but as it stands, Mistria already has my heart."
title: Fields of Mistria 1.0 Review

author: IGN
description:
Hellraiser: Revival reviewed by Tristan Ogilvie on PlayStation 5. Also available on Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.

"As someone who’s been seriously spooked by the Hellraiser movies since I was barely tall enough to reach them on the top shelf of my local video store, I certainly got some thrills from staring down cenobites in Hellraiser: Revival as I stalked the cold, concrete chambers of the sprawling otherworld labyrinth that they call home. Its combat is derivative but solid enough to serve up a satisfying amount of slaughter, and some of the not-safe-for-work (or home) puzzles are certainly memorable, if not particularly challenging. However, Revival often struggles to sustain tension, with enemy encounters that are all too easily manipulated, a story propped up by too much telling and not enough showing, and obnoxiously repeated boss fights and chase sequences that make its nine-hour runtime suffer from more bloat than Butterball’s belly. title: Hellraiser: Revival Review
